purpose: Auto3dgm allows for comparative analysis of 3D digital models representing biological surfaces using fully automated landmark placement and alignment within 3D Slicer.
summary: Auto3dgm is a 3D Slicer extension for automated 3D geometric morphometric analysis and alignment of surfaces. Inspection of the source code, CMake configuration, and catalog entry reveals clean packaging, proper adherence to Slicer scripted module conventions, and explicit user confirmation for third-party package installation (`mosek`). No safety or packaging issues were identified. 🟢 Recommend merge

safety.rationale: Inspected widget initialization, file loading, and export functions. No unauthorized telemetry, remote code execution, command injection, or unsafe deserialization found.

environment.rationale: Package installation (`pip_install('mosek')`) occurs on widget initialization inside a confirmation dialog (`slicer.util.confirmOkCancelDisplay`), with no silent startup installation or changes to core bundled Slicer packages.

packaging.rationale: CMake correctly installs scripted modules, resources, and directories (`auto3dgm_nazar` and `meshviewer`). Catalog entry is valid and matches build setup.

license.rationale: MIT license provided under Auto3dgm/auto3dgm_nazar/LICENSE and standard Slicer licensing terms.

soundness.rationale: Properly uses Slicer ScriptedLoadableModule structures, VTK objects, and NumPy arrays. Methods handle errors and utilize Slicer utility functions appropriately.

utility.rationale: Provides automated 3D geometric morphometrics functionality with GUI tabs, visualization tools, documentation links, and tests.

findings.title: Commercial/Academic dependency on MOSEK
findings.explanation: The extension requires the commercial optimization package MOSEK and an external license file to perform core correspondence analysis, which may limit out-of-the-box usability for community users without academic licenses.
findings.suggestion: Ensure users are well-informed about the MOSEK dependency and licensing requirements in the documentation.

not_checked: Test fixtures and execution of heavy numerical routines
